title: Man killed in Toronto police shooting at downtown building identified
subtitle: Police investigating missing person when Gedi Ali Gedi was shot
article: The province's Special Investigations Unit (SIU) has released the identity of a 45-year-old man fatally shot by Toronto police on Feb. 23.

At about 3:30 a.m. Tuesday morning, Gedi Ali Gedi was involved in a deadly interaction with two officers in a third-floor unit of a Toronto Community Housing building at 291 George St., which is between Dundas and Gerrard streets in the Garden District.

Interim Toronto Police Chief James Ramer said, at the time of the incident, investigators were "simultaneously conducting a homicide investigation as a result of a person who was reported missing earlier."
Police said while investigating they encountered a man with a gun, which led to an exchange that resulted in them opening fire on him.

Gedi, whose next of kin consented to releasing his name, was transported to hospital with life-threatening injuries. He was pronounced dead there at 4:17 a.m. A post-mortem examination for Gedi took place Feb. 24.
The SIU, which is investigating, said they collected two police-issued firearms from the scene. Investigators also located two edged weapons and video evidence, the agency said.
Five investigators and three forensic investigators have now been assigned to this case. The agency has also dedicated two subject officials as well as seven witness officials to this investigation.
Anyone with information is urged to contact the lead investigator at 1-800-787-8529. Those with video evidence related to this incident are also asked to upload it through the SIU website.
